Q: Set Quarto chunk options such as fig-height from an R object or expression A:

Use !expr in Quarto chunk options to provide values from your environment as options. This way you can calculate the height based on your data, and pass the value to the fig-height option. You need to render the Quarto document to see the resulting height.

Here is a reproducible example:

---
title: "Plot height test"
format: 
  html:
    embed-resources: true
---

With parametrized Quarto reports, certain figures are expected to grow or shrink in widht/height based on existing data. This Quarto report demonstrates how to automatically adjust figure height based on the number of rows present in data. A horizontal column plot (where Y values are groups and X values are a continuous variable, so that bars grow sideways) of fixed height would simply shrink all columns to make them fit in the default height, but in this example, the plot height itself will increase according to the number of rows, so that all plots will have roughly the same column widths.

```{r setup}
library(ggplot2)

rows <- 23
```

Data will have `{r} rows` rows.

```{r data}
data <- data.frame(
  group = letters[1:rows],
  values = sample(10:90, rows, replace = TRUE)
)
```

```{r height}
base <- 0.3
height <- base * nrow(data)
```

Based on `{r} nrow(data)` rows, with a base height of `{r} base` per row, plot height will be `{r} height`.

```{r plot}
#| fig-height: !expr height
#| fig-width: 5
data |> 
  ggplot() +
  aes(values, group) +
  geom_col() +
  theme_classic()
```

Q: Using ld on macOS to turn a raw arm64 binary into an executable Mach-O binary A:

If you have a symbol in the output.bin machine code, it can be called from a program with _main.

Example: output.bin is a Hello, World! program.

% nm output.bin  
0000000000000000 T \_hello  
0000000000000024 t helloworld  
0000000000000000 t ltmp0

This tells us our outer symbol name is _hello and that its internal function was called helloworld.

So, create the entry.s stub to load the symbol.

.global _main
.text
.p2align 2
_main:
    stp x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
    mov x29, sp
    bl _hello
    mov w0, #0
    ldp x29, x30, [sp], #16
    ret

Then compile it, link them, and execute:

% clang -c entry.s -o entry.o
% clang entry.o output.bin -o entry
% ./entry
Hello, World!

Q: org.apache.openejb.config.ValidationFailedException: Module failed validation. AppModule(name=appname) TomEE A:

The message really describes wide variety of meanings. In my case there it has been written in log-file and nothing more distinct except "SEVERE [main] org.apache.openejb.config.ReportValidationResults.logResults ERROR ... null: Cannot validate jar: ...". But in console there was more clear notice "java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: ..." So check logs and console together.

Q: ADB shell script to send AT commands to a modem-cannot return control to a shell and capture output A:

I had similar problems with redirecting output to file. I resolved my problem by adding CMD /c in front of the echo command. I.e. if I understand correctly you need to tell the system that it needs to wait until command finishes executing and only then redirect output to a file. I was doing it in DOS.

Since you are running on ANDROID try adding sh -c in front of your command. Hope it helps.
